highlights: From 2 Aug 2026 the EU AI Office + national authorities began enforcing the AI Act; chatbots must disclose they are AI, deepfakes must be labelled, AI content needs machine-readable marks. 180+ orgs signed the transparency Code of Practice.
Citizens now have two live EU channels: the AI Act complaints tool and the AI Act whistleblower tool.

The Digital Omnibus (in force 27 Jul 2026) pushed strict high-risk obligations to 2 Dec 2027 — incl. conformity assessment, public EU registration and the fundamental-rights impact assessment for public authorities. GDPR Art. 22 remains the main protection until then.
Palantir police software: BVerfG has limited automated police data analysis; NRW's Palantir law criticised as unconstitutional (netzpolitik, 21.04.2026); constitutional complaint pending in Bavaria.
CJEU C-634/21 (SCHUFA): generating a credit score is itself an automated decision under Art. 22 GDPR where lenders draw strongly on it — extends to recruitment, insurance, health.
Mobley v. Workday: US court granted preliminary collective certification over age-biased AI applicant screening and treated the AI tool as an 'agent' of the employer.
